summary: Gives examples of how iSCSI names are built and discusses how initiators find iSCSI targets. It aims for flexibility, serving both small isolated setups and large environments that need secure, scalable discovery. It complements the main iSCSI document and was updated by RFC 7143.

eli5.summary: Before a computer can use a network disk, it has to know the disk's name and where to find it. This note shows how to name things and how to look them up.

subtitle: Worked examples of how iSCSI names are built, what aliases are for, and how initiators find targets.

tldr.problem: iSCSI initiators and targets need stable names so storage can be managed wherever it sits, and initiators need ways to find targets that suit both small and large setups.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC gives examples of the iqn. and eui. name formats, explains optional human-friendly aliases, and describes three discovery methods: static configuration, SendTargets and zero-configuration.
tldr.outcome: It complements the main iSCSI document, RFC 3720, and was updated by RFC 7143. The appendices cover proxies, firewalls and the link between names and security identities.

today: RFC 3721 is an Informational document that was updated by RFC 7143. It complements the main iSCSI specification, RFC 3720.

sections.title: iSCSI Names and Addresses
sections.content:
The main addressable entity in iSCSI is the iSCSI node, which can be an initiator, a target or both. The rules for building names are in RFC 3720; this RFC supplies examples a naming authority might follow. An iSCSI name is the unique identifier of the node and also its SCSI device name, and it is the principal object used for authentication. Names belong to nodes rather than to network adapter cards, so an adapter can move between hosts without losing SCSI state such as reservations or authorization configuration.

Names and addresses are kept separate. A name is a location-independent, permanent identifier, one per node for its whole life. An address is the name plus a TCP location in the form <domain-name>[:<port>], where the domain name is an IPv4 address, a bracketed IPv6 address or a fully qualified domain name. For targets the port is optional and defaults to 3260, the port assigned by IANA. A node can have any number of addresses, which may change at any time, for instance when assigned by DHCP.

The RFC compares this to a person: a unique identifier (like the name), plus phone numbers and street addresses (like the TCP addresses), plus a friendly name like "Robert Smith" (like the alias).
sections.eli5: Your name stays the same even when you move. Your address changes when you move house. iSCSI keeps the two apart so a disk can be found at a new address and still be the same disk.

sections.title: Building iqn. and eui. Names
sections.content:
An iSCSI qualified name (iqn.) holds, in order, the string iqn., a year-and-month date code for when the naming authority registered its domain, the authority string as a reversed domain name, and optionally a colon followed by a string chosen by the assigning organization. In iqn.2001-04.com.example:diskarrays-sn-a8675309, the date guards against domain names being sold or transferred, com.example is the naming authority, and the rest is whatever example.com chose to keep names unique.

The scheme lets an authority hand out sub-spaces. The two names iqn.2001-04.com.example.storage:tape.sys1.xyz and iqn.2001-04.com.example.storage.tape:sys1.xyz differ only in the colon position, and both are legal and unique because different subdomain owners assigned them. Other examples cover a university user and a storage service provider that renames targets by customer and disk number. The first component after iqn. must be a top-level domain such as com or a two-letter country code, and companies must not drop their com..

These names are not addresses. The domain name only identifies the naming authority and implies nothing about location.

The eui. format uses an IEEE EUI-64 identifier written as ASCII hexadecimal, for example eui.02004567A425678D.
sections.eli5: An iqn. name is like a mailing label that says which company made the name, when they got their website name, and then a code only that company uses. Nobody can make the same label twice because each company owns its own part.

sections.title: Aliases
sections.content:
An alias is an optional UTF-8 string that describes an initiator or target. It need not be unique, and it must NOT be used to identify, address or authenticate either side or to select a target at login. It is a variable-length string of 0 to 255 characters, terminated with at least one NULL (0x00) character, as defined in RFC 3720. The two sides exchange aliases at login.

The value is in user interfaces. A list of names like iqn.1995-04.com.example:sn.5551212.target.450 says little, whereas an alias such as "Oracle 1" shows at a glance whether the right target is connected. Targets send a TargetAlias alongside TargetName, and initiators send an InitiatorAlias alongside InitiatorName. Simple devices may skip aliases: an alias that is unwanted, does not fit or seems invalid is simply ignored. An initiator alias is often just the hostname, though a description of the machine's job is better.
sections.eli5: An alias is a nickname, like writing "Grandma" next to a long phone number. It helps people, but the computers never rely on it to decide who is who.

sections.title: How Initiators Discover Targets
sections.content:
The goal of discovery is low overhead for small setups and scalability for large ones. The RFC lists three mechanisms, differing in how much the initiator already knows.

  • Static configuration: the initiator already has the IP address, TCP port and target name, so it does no discovery. This suits small setups.
  • SendTargets: the initiator knows the address and port of a Network Entity, opens a discovery session and issues the SendTargets text command (defined in RFC 3720) to ask which targets are there. This suits iSCSI gateways and routers.
  • Zero-configuration: the initiator knows nothing, and either multicasts discovery messages or asks storage name servers. The RFC says SLP can clearly perform the needed discovery functions, and iSNS can add management functions such as notification and access management. Equipment needing more than SendTargets should at least implement SLP, and consider iSNS for larger storage networks.
sections.eli5: You can have a written list of where every disk is, ask one front desk for a list of what it has, or shout into the room and see who answers.

sections.title: Proxies, Firewalls and Security Identifiers
sections.content:
Appendix B explains that iSCSI should work through intermediaries because access and scaling problems arise if the whole Internet is used as one storage network. A port redirector (stateless NAT) means iSCSI data integrity checks must not cover TCP or IP header information, messages should name nodes by iSCSI name, and a target behind one should return a domain name instead of an IP address in a SendTargets response. A SOCKS server usually listens on port 1080 and needs a modified initiator. A SCSI gateway presents logical targets and must keep any iSCSI names it makes unique. An iSCSI proxy ends iSCSI on both sides, so header and data integrity checks should be separate to allow end-to-end data checks. A stateful inspection firewall is invisible to the initiator and is effective only outbound unless the target is in a DMZ.

Appendix C separates the node name from a security identifier. In trusted environments an access control list of node names may be enough. In untrusted ones the initiator also passes an identifier such as a userid to an authentication process like SRP, CHAP or Kerberos, and the target must check that this identity may use the claimed InitiatorName. Its example is that 'Frank' authorized for one initiator name must be rejected if he logs in with another.
sections.eli5: Sometimes a guard or a switchboard sits between you and the disk. Because the disk's name never changes, the guard can pass messages along without confusion. And knowing someone's name is not enough, they also have to prove it is really them.
